This project uses the 2024 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) — the largest continuously conducted health telephone survey in the world, with 457,670 respondents across 49 states, DC, and US territories — to model the odds of a diabetes diagnosis as a function of demographic, behavioural, and social determinant predictors in a nationally representative US adult sample.

The project is organised into three parts:

---

## Overview

A concise summary of the analysis, headline odds ratios, and the most important visualisations.

↗ [Open Overview »](analysis/overview.qmd)

---

## Exploratory Data Analysis

Sample characteristics, variable distributions, outcome prevalence by subgroup, and unadjusted associations.

↗ [Open EDA »](analysis/eda.qmd)

---

## Logistic Regression

Full model specification, complete case exclusions, VIF checks, diagnostics, ROC/AUC, Hosmer-Lemeshow, and the OR table.

↗ [Open Regression »](analysis/logistic-regression.qmd)
